articles.title: Rand Paul Formally Accuses Fauci of Perjury — Demands DOJ Investigate COVID Origins Testimony
articles.summary: Senator Rand Paul has filed a formal request with the Department of Justice to investigate Dr. Anthony Fauci for allegedly lying under oath during 2021 congressional testimony about NIH funding of gain-of-function research. Paul argues Fauci knowingly misled Congress when he denied NIH involvement in risky coronavirus experiments at the Wuhan Institute of Virology. If substantiated, this represents one of the most consequential acts of institutional deception in the history of American public health.

articles.title: Fauci's Secret Diary: Trump Contempt, China Praise, and Classified Files Lost in Ransomware Attack
articles.summary: Newly released diary pages from Dr. Anthony Fauci reveal he privately disparaged President Trump while publicly praising Chinese health officials during the pandemic — raising serious questions about whose interests he was serving. The diary also discloses that a set of confidential government records was lost in a ransomware hack, a security failure never disclosed to the public. This is the internal record of a man who shaped global pandemic policy while apparently operating with deeply conflicted loyalties.

articles.title: Off-Patent, Dirt-Cheap Drugs Like Ivermectin Are Showing Real Cancer Results — Oncology's Profit Motive Buries Them
articles.summary: Dr. William Makis argues that repurposed off-patent drugs including ivermectin demonstrate legitimate anti-cancer mechanisms that the oncology establishment refuses to seriously investigate because there is no profit in doing so. Standard-of-care cancer treatment generates billions annually for pharma, creating a structural incentive to suppress low-cost alternatives regardless of their efficacy signals. Makis names the system directly: cancer patients are being abandoned not for lack of options, but for lack of financial motive to explore them.

articles.title: Antidepressants: What the Mainstream Won't Print About Benefits, Harms, and the Science Behind Both
articles.summary: A critical analysis of antidepressant medications examines the growing disconnect between their explosive prescription rates and the actual evidence base for their efficacy and safety. The piece confronts the chemical imbalance hypothesis — still used to market SSRIs — despite its having been quietly abandoned by mainstream psychiatry. With antidepressants now among the most prescribed drug classes in the world, the gap between what patients are told and what the data shows represents a systemic failure of informed consent.

articles.title: Medical Device Maker Beta Bionics Allegedly Hid Safety Failures from Investors — FDA Compliance Crisis Explodes
articles.summary: A securities fraud class action alleges that Beta Bionics misled investors about the safety, efficacy, and commercial viability of its iLet medical device, triggering a 37% stock collapse when the truth emerged. The case raises urgent questions about how long the company's FDA compliance failures were known internally before disclosure — and who in the regulatory chain may have been aware. This is the anatomy of a medical device cover-up with real patients on the other end of a malfunctioning product.

articles.title: Plano COVID Clinics Bilked Federal Programs for $20 Million — Billed Nasal Swabs as Full Office Visits
articles.summary: A network of COVID testing clinics in Plano, Texas has agreed to pay $20 million to settle allegations that they systematically billed nasal swab tests as full physician office visits, defrauding federal uninsured-patient relief programs. The scheme exploited the emergency infrastructure built around COVID to extract maximum reimbursement with minimal care delivered. This is COVID fraud at the clinical level — and it was the uninsured, most vulnerable patients whose program funds were looted.

articles.title: Epstein Whistleblower Found Dead — His Exposure of Lutnick Links Preceded Abrupt 'Suicide'
articles.summary: A British whistleblower who helped surface previously undisclosed connections between Jeffrey Epstein and U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick died by apparent suicide, triggering immediate calls for an independent investigation into how UK regulators treated him in the lead-up to his death. Critics are asking whether the pressure applied to this source played a role in his death — and why the Epstein-Lutnick links he exposed received so little mainstream scrutiny. Whistleblowers keep dying; the people they expose keep thriving.

articles.title: Repurposed Cancer Drug Mebendazole Overcomes Gefitinib Resistance in Lung Cancer — Pharma Has No Interest
articles.summary: A peer-reviewed study published in PLOS ONE demonstrates that mebendazole, a decades-old antiparasitic drug costing pennies per dose, can overcome acquired resistance to gefitinib in EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer by disrupting microtubule dynamics and amplifying replication stress. Gefitinib resistance is a major — and enormously profitable — problem that oncology currently addresses with expensive next-generation targeted therapies. A cheap repurposed drug solving that problem has no champion in a system built on patent-protected revenues.

articles.title: Fauci Perjury Exposed: Rand Paul Demands DOJ Prosecute America's COVID Czar for Lying to Congress About Gain-of-Function Funding

articles.title: Fauci's Secret Diary Surfaces: He Trashed Trump, Praised China, and Lost Classified Files in a Ransomware Attack
articles.summary: Newly released diary pages from Dr. Anthony Fauci reveal he privately disparaged President Trump while publicly projecting institutional neutrality, praised Chinese health officials during a period when China was actively suppressing COVID-19 origin data, and lost a cache of confidential government records in a ransomware hack. The diary provides fresh ammunition for investigators probing whether Fauci's policy decisions were driven by politics and foreign deference rather than public health science.

articles.title: The Antidepressant Reckoning: What the Medical Establishment Still Won't Tell You About the Drugs It Prescribes to Millions
articles.summary: A new analysis published via Spektrum's SciLogs platform forces a direct confrontation with the inconvenient evidence on antidepressants — a drug class prescribed to hundreds of millions worldwide despite persistent scientific disputes over efficacy, dependency risk, and long-term neurological harm. The piece examines the gap between the 'chemical imbalance' marketing narrative that launched the SSRI era and the far murkier reality documented in clinical literature. With antidepressant prescriptions still rising globally, the failure to honestly communicate both benefits and harms to patients represents a systemic informed-consent crisis.

articles.title: Oncologist Dr. Makis Goes on Record: Cheap Off-Patent Drugs Like Ivermectin May Work Against Cancer — and Big Pharma Knows It

The suppression of this research is not accidental — a single cheap generic drug eliminating cancer would collapse a multi-hundred-billion-dollar treatment industry built on patent-protected chemotherapy and biologics. Makis names the system directly, and the data he cites deserves peer scrutiny, not media blackout.

articles.title: Beta Bionics Hid FDA Safety Problems From Investors — Now a Securities Fraud Lawsuit Exposes the Cover-Up
articles.summary: A securities fraud class action lawsuit alleges that Beta Bionics systematically misled investors about the safety, efficacy, and regulatory standing of its iLet automated insulin delivery device, withholding material FDA compliance problems until the stock collapsed by 37%. This is the pharma-device playbook: generate investor capital on manipulated safety narratives, let insiders exit, then let retail investors absorb the crash when regulators finally force disclosure. The iLet case raises urgent questions about whether the FDA's pre-market oversight failed patients before it failed shareholders.

articles.title: COVID Billing Fraud: Plano Clinics Pocketed $20 Million Billing Nose Swabs as Full Office Visits — Federal Taxpayers Foot the Bill
articles.summary: Heal 360 COVID testing clinics in Plano, Texas, have agreed to pay $20 million to settle federal allegations that they fraudulently billed nasal swab tests as comprehensive office visits, exploiting emergency government healthcare funding designed for the uninsured. This is not an isolated compliance failure — it is a window into the industrialized fraud that consumed billions in pandemic emergency spending while real patients were denied care. The settlement confirms what investigators warned from the start: rushed, oversight-free COVID funding programs were an open invitation to systematic theft.

articles.title: Repurposed Drug Mebendazole Suppresses Drug-Resistant Lung Cancer Tumors — Why Is Oncology Still Ignoring It?
articles.summary: A peer-reviewed study published in PLOS ONE demonstrates that mebendazole, a decades-old antiparasitic drug costing pennies per dose, significantly suppresses tumor growth in gefitinib-resistant non-small cell lung cancer by disrupting microtubule dynamics and amplifying replication stress in cancer cells. This research adds to a growing body of evidence that off-patent antiparasitic and antimicrobial drugs have legitimate anticancer mechanisms — evidence that receives a fraction of the funding and media attention directed at patent-protected biologics costing $100,000 per treatment course. The oncology establishment's silence on this data is not scientific; it is financial.
